name: Buzi
overview: Buzi is a male member of the tribe of Levi, known primarily as a priest and the father of the prophet Ezekiel. His role as a Levite and priest situates him within the religious leadership of Israel during the prophetic era. Beyond this, Scripture provides limited additional details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Buzi means 'contempt' in Hebrew. This proper name, mentioned in Ezekiel 1:3, reflects the original biblical designation without indication that it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Buzi as the father of Ezekiel, the well-known prophet. No other family relationships are detailed beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Buzi's significance in the biblical narrative is closely tied to his identity as a priest and the father of Ezekiel. Through his lineage, Buzi is connected to the prophetic ministry that called Israel to repentance and faithfulness to God. His priestly heritage underscores the spiritual context from which Ezekiel emerged as a divinely appointed messenger.
